choices.content: If two lines are parallel, their alternate interior angles are equal
If alternate interior angles are equal, the two lines are parallel
If two lines are parallel, their same-side interior angles are supplementary

question.prompt: In a proof, the statement “Since \(AB\parallel CD\) (\(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are alternate interior angles formed when lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) are cut by a third line), it follows that \(\angle 1=\angle 2\)” is based on:

solutions.explanation: Deducing that alternate interior angles are equal from the given parallel lines uses the property of parallel lines: if two lines are parallel, their alternate interior angles are equal.
solutions.title: Identify the parallel-line property
